Lorna Risbourne: Richard and Ormonde met at a dance on April 26th 1915. Richard had been interned as a prisoner of war in India when he was only 19. The consular staff refused to issue a passport to him because he was too young and so he set sail from Calcutta for Ceylon with the first boat. He had not gone more than a month before the ship was torpedoed and he was fortunate to be rescued. He was now age 20, legally too young to enter England, so Richard left India for Ceylon. It was in Ceylon where he met Ormonde

In the winter of 1898/99, Georges Thenault published his Etudes Caractéristiques (that have now become known as the Cinématographie). These lessons formed the basis of the formation of a cinematograph exchange program between France and Greece. In March 1900, Thenault and the French Technical Mission visited Athens to present the cinematograph for the first time in Greece.
